answer: Each agent registers a hash of its fine-tuned model weights: the fingerprint bridges identity and computation, and clones sharing one model cannot register twice. Each epoch the network demands a random 1 MB weight shard; the verifier recomputes its hash, and any mismatch revokes the identity. A Sybil farm must fine-tune 100 distinct models for 100 identities; each costs $40 of GPU time plus 6 hours, so 100 clones cost $4,000 and 600 hours. Sybil farms drift like a glacier of identical copies that the shard audit spots; every clone stands on a narrow ledge, and one failed check ends it.
